Apple today expanded Apple Music to four more countries, bringing the service to a total of 172 countries and regions worldwide. Details below.

Apple Music officially launches in four new countries

As discovered by Aaron Perris on X, Apple updated its support page for the availability of its Apple media services today, expanding Apple Music availability to Albania, Brunei, Burkina Faso, and Pakistan.

Perhaps not coincidentally, three of the four new countries also appear on the list of regions where Apple previously announced free access to Apple TV+ and Apple Arcade for iCloud+ subscribers. The sole exception is Brunei, where Apple TV+ subscription service remains unavailable.

This expansion also coincides with a major update to the Apple Music Android app, with version 7.0 launching in beta, featuring a brand-new Liquid Glass redesign, a floating bottom navigation bar, a mini player, and more.

Additionally, this expansion comes after Apple rolled out Apple Pay support in India, reflecting the company's ongoing efforts to expand its services business into new markets — a move likely aimed at addressing slowing growth in services revenue.

For the full official list of Apple's global media service availability, click here.

Apple Music requires an active subscription, priced at US$11.99 per month with the first month free, or available through an Apple One bundle.
